# UNDERWRITING MEMORANDUM — Chagee Holdings Limited (CHA)

## SECTION 0. Overview

| Bull IV | **$22.80** → MoS **+108%** | [Estimate] |

**The one-line thesis:** The market is pricing CHA as a *permanently shrinking* business — the neutral reverse DCF implies a **-1.8% 10-yr CAGR** (below even the p50 base rate of 5.6% for this size bucket) — while the filings show a structurally lower cost base (SBC step-down, headcount cuts, non-repeating IPO fees) that lifted Q2 2026 GAAP net margin to **13.6% vs 2.3% a year earlier**, a same-store decline *narrowing* from -27.8% to -16.1%, overseas GMV compounding at **+114.3% YoY**, and ~**US$1.09B of net cash** that alone is worth ~$5.70/share. Every one of my three scenarios sits *above* the price because the business is worth ~$7/share even in the Bear, on top of the net-cash floor.

---

## SECTION 1. Macro
From DATA 1.5 / 1.6 (as of 2026-10-04):
- **Rates:** rf (nominal 10y) **5.24%**, real 2.88%, breakeven 2.36%; curve 10y-2y +0.45% (Normal/Steepening); IG spread 1.49%, HY OAS 3.24%. The COE ANCHOR is **10.04%** (rf_eff 5.24% + Blume-adjusted loading 1.149× × market-consistent premium 4.17%).
- **Regime vector:** goldilocks 0.341 / reflation 0.271 / tightening 0.176 / stagflation 0.130 / recession 0.081 — headline goldilocks but **contested** (margin 0.070).
- **Inflation:** CPI YoY 3.35%, PCE YoY 3.42% — sticky.
- **Active shock:** `oil_shock` (severity 1, direction up, onset 2026-09-28) via the Strait of Hormuz closure and Saudi pipeline attacks; China suspended most October refined-fuel exports (2026-10-01).

**Exposure:** CHA is a PRC consumer-discretionary. The macro hits it through three channels: (1) **high rates** keep the discount rate elevated (10.04% anchor) and cap multiples; (2) **sticky inflation + oil shock** squeeze the discretionary tea-drink consumer and raise logistics/energy costs for 883 company-owned teahouses; (3) the **contested-regime / recession tail (0.081)** plus a China retail-sales slowdown (Aug data: retail +0.4% y/y, per DATA 1.6) is the demand risk that keeps Greater China SSS negative. The oil shock is a second-order cost headwind, not a core driver — I carry it in the Bear's margin path, not as a standalone scenario.

---

## SECTION 2. Business & Moat
**Economic engines (mandate 1):**
- **(a) Transactional franchise deliveries (the core, ~72.5% of Q2 revenue):** Franchised teahouses (6,756) pay royalty/supply revenue. This is the shrinking engine — Q2 2026 franchise net revenue **RMB 2,474.0M vs RMB 3,020.7M y/y (-18%)** [Actual, PRIMARY P1], driven by Greater China GMV falling to RMB 7,156.3M from RMB 7,867.9M and per-store monthly GMV slipping to **RMB 338,259 from RMB 356,080** [Actual, PRIMARY P1].
- **(b) Company-owned + overseas (the growth engine, ~27.5% of Q2 revenue):** Company-owned teahouse revenue **RMB 940.6M vs RMB 311.2M y/y (+202%)** [Actual, PRIMARY P1] as the mix shifts to owned stores (883 total, 259 overseas) and overseas GMV hits **RMB 504.0M (+114.3% YoY)** across 8 markets [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. This is higher-margin (full cup revenue recognized) but small (~6.6% of GMV) — real optionality, not yet the base case.
- **(c) Strategic optionality:** International expansion (Korea debut: 3 teahouses sold >16,000 cups in first 3 days; 46,000 pre-open app downloads [Unconfirmed — third-party]), single-origin Yunnan tea supply chain (>10,000 tons/yr [Unconfirmed — research brief]), and a 47.1M-member app ecosystem [Actual, PRIMARY P1].

**Owner earnings after SBC (mandate 2):** I treat SBC as a real cost, **deducted in cash flow once** (`sbc_treatment = deducted_in_cf`). FY2025 filed SBC was **US$0.103B** [Actual, DATA 5] — heavy, and the single biggest reason FY2025 owner earnings were depressed at **~US$0.097B** (the DEFAULTS base). H1 2026 SBC collapsed (G&A SBC down RMB 482.7M y/y in Q2 alone [Actual, PRIMARY P1]), which is why H1 2026 net income attributable jumped to **US$135.2M vs US$74.8M (+81%)** [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. My Base grows the depressed FY2025 base +55% in year 1 to reflect this genuine step-up, then decelerates.

**Moat rating (seven factors, 0-3 each; total 9/21 → 2.7/5.0):**
| Factor | Score | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Brand & product differentiation | 2 | Premium "BOYA" tea latte, single-origin sourcing; but intense competition (Mixue/Heytea/Nayuki) |
| Scale & cost advantage | 2 | 7,639 stores [Actual], vertical tea supply chain, franchise leverage |
| Switching costs | 1 | Low — beverages switch easily |
| Network effects | 1 | 47.1M members / app data; weak |
| Intangibles / IP | 1 | Brand + recipes, lightly patented |
| Regulatory moat | 0 | None — the Cayman/PRC structure is a *risk*, not a moat |
| Distribution (franchise network) | 2 | 6,756 franchised teahouses are a real distribution asset |

**Direction: stable-to-narrowing domestically** (franchise revenue -18% YoY), **building internationally**. Net-cash balance sheet (US$963.9M cash + time deposits/short-term investments vs only US$27.4M short-term borrowings as of 2026-06-30 [Actual, PRIMARY P1]) is a genuine financial-strength plus and the source of the valuation floor.

## SECTION 3. Valuation
**Frame:** Equity frame — every flow in the pack is after-interest; net debt is negative (net cash), so the firm frame is refused/inappropriate. Discount rate = COE ANCHOR **10.04%** for Base/Bull; **12.0%** for Bear (+196 bp cost-of-capital shock, within mandate 4's +100-200 bp band).

**Desk inputs I chose (and departures from DEFAULTS):**
| Input | My value | Default | Departure reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| base_cf | $0.097B | $0.097B | None (within 2% of owner_earnings_default_b) |
| Base growth y1-y5 | +55% / +15% / +10% / +7% / +5% | consensus-derived | **guidance_deviation_reason:** the consensus year-1/2 levels are built by applying unreliable RMB-basis EPS growth to the depressed FY2025 base; the filings show a structural step-up (H1 2026 NI attributable US$135.2M vs US$74.8M, Q2 op income +387.6% YoY) |
| Fade years | 5 | — | Declared fade from explicit path to terminal |
| terminal_g | 3.75% | 3.75% | None (long-run nominal anchor) |
| terminal_ronic | 10.04% (=COE) | 10.04% | None — my record holds <3 years of ROIC, so new investment earns no more than its cost; growth adds no value beyond year 5 |
| Shares | 190,763,326 (default) | same | Dilution factor 1.0083 < 1.05, so not applied |
| Excess cash | $1.088B (default, FY2025 base) | same | Desk adds per share to every scenario; ~$5.70/share floor |
| Cash-flow life | Perpetual | — | Brand/store network renewable out of deducted capex; no filed reserves/licence expiry |

**Terminal & implied multiple (mandate 3):** With terminal_ronic = COE, the terminal is a Gordon perpetuity on year-5 owner earnings at g=3.75%: implied terminal multiple = (1+g)/(r−g) = 1.0375/(0.1004−0.0375) ≈ **16.5×** on year-5 cash flow. Cross-check vs peers: cluster trailing P/E median **19.8×**, MRI sector median **16.9×** (DATA 8.5). My ~16.5× terminal multiple is **at/below the peer band** — I am not paying up for growth; the value comes from the depressed base + net cash, not an aggressive terminal. Gap to cluster median ≈ -3.3 turns.

**Neutral reverse DCF (mandate 3b):** Under the neutral structure (anchor COE, 10-yr fade), the current price implies a **-1.78% 10-year CAGR**. For a $1-10B company the base-rate band is **median 5.6%, p90 16.7%** (5-yr sustained). The market-implied -1.78% is *below the p50* — it prices CHA as a structurally shrinking, value-destroying business. My Base grows ~+7.3%/yr in years 3-5 fading to 3.75%, i.e., **~9 points above what the price implies**. That gap is my disagreement, and it is supported by dated filings (below), not a cap.

**The two cruxes (my stated disagreement with the price):**
1. **growth_years_3_5 — mine +7.3%/yr vs price-implied -32.0%/yr.** The price implies cash flow *halving* over the explicit window. The filings contradict this: same-store GMV growth narrowed from **-27.8% (Sep-2025) to -16.1% (Jun-2026)** and overseas GMV grew **+114.3% YoY** [PRIMARY P1, 2026-08-28]. A business whose SSS is *improving* at a sharp clip and whose second engine is doubling is not one whose cash flow compounds at -32%/yr.
2. **coe — mine 10.04% vs price-implied 24.85%.** The price implies a ~25% discount rate (distressed-credit territory). CHA is **net cash** (US$963.9M cash + time deposits/ST investments vs US$27.4M short-term borrowings, 2026-06-30 [PRIMARY P1]) with an asset-light franchise model (72.5% of Q2 revenue franchised). A 24.85% COE is not supportable for a net-cash, low-leverage consumer brand; the correct rate is the 10.04% anchor.

**Reconciliation of DCF vs market multiples:** The stock trades at ~7.6× forward P/E (catalyst brief) vs a $15.04 consensus mean target and cluster median 19.8× trailing. My Base of $19.24 sits *above* the consensus mean target — but that is because I (a) credit the full net-cash position, (b) start from a depressed base that steps up structurally, and (c) do not clamp the terminal. The honest read: the multiple gap to peers is real but mostly explained by the demand headwind the market is rationally pricing; my edge is that the *cash floor + margin step-up* put even the Bear above the price.

## SECTION 7. Risks
- **Domestic shrinkage is structural, not cyclical:** If Greater China SSS does *not* inflect (the -16.1% keeps going), franchise revenue (-18% YoY in Q2) erodes the base and margin can't outrun it. This is the primary risk and the Bear's core.
- **Margin step-up is partly non-recurring:** A large share of the 13.6% net margin is SBC step-down, one-time restructuring, and non-repeating IPO professional fees. If SBC normalizes or competition forces price concessions, margin mean-reverts.
- **Competition / pricing power:** Intense industry competition (management's own words in PRIMARY P1) in a category with near-zero switching costs; single-origin sourcing is a differentiator but not a barrier.
- **Overseas unit economics:** 8 markets, mostly sub-scale; new-market fixed costs and supply-chain stretch could make the "growth engine" margin-dilutive before it is material (only ~6.6% of GMV).
- **Structural / regulatory:** Cayman-incorporated, PRC-operating; VIE-like cross-border governance, data-privacy and tax-compliance exposure; a securities-fraud investigation was referenced in third-party sources [Unconfirmed] — I could not verify it against the filings and do not credit it as fact, but it is a reputational tail.
- **Currency / ADR:** RMB reporting vs USD ADR; FX moves the per-share math.

**Pre-mortem ("we lost 50% of the capital in five years — what went wrong?"):** Q3 (Nov) showed August SSS *missed* the positive guide and re-deepened to -20%+; franchise net closures accelerated through H2 2026; a price war forced operating margin back toward single digits; overseas markets posted negative unit economics and were scaled back; and the net-cash cushion was consumed by a buyback that stopped supporting the price. The stock then de-rated from $11 to ~$5-6 as the market realized the "margin step-up" was one-off and the top line was structurally shrinking — i.e., the Bear *and* a below-Bear outcome, which my net-cash floor only partially protects against if cash is returned rather than held.

## SECTION 9. Red Team
**Strongest short thesis:** "CHA is a shrinking, low-switching-cost tea franchise in a price war. The 13.6% net margin is an accounting artifact of a one-time SBC write-down and restructuring charges that won't repeat; strip those out and the business earns a mid-single-digit margin on a top line falling ~5-8%/yr. The 'overseas engine' is 6.6% of GMV in sub-scale markets with unproven unit economics. You're paying $11 for a business whose cash flow is *declining*, and the only reason it isn't worth less is ~$1B of cash that management will return or squander. The correct value is the net cash plus a low multiple on shrinking earnings — i.e., $8-9, not $19."

**My answer:** (1) I *agree* the margin step-up is largely cost arithmetic — which is exactly why my Base grows from margin, not volume, and why I do not extrapolate 13.6% net margin forever; my terminal holds new investment at just its cost of capital (terminal_ronic = COE), so I am not paying for a margin that won't repeat. (2) I *disagree* the cash flow is declining: the SSS trajectory (-27.8% → -16.1%) is improving, and the company is *already* net cash — the short's $8-9 "cash-plus" value is below my Bear of $12.83 because it under-multiple a business still generating ~$0.1B+ of owner earnings at a 10% rate. (3) The real test is the Q3 SSS print; if it fails, I am already positioned to the Bear (and the starter-only sizing means limited exposure until then). The short thesis is strongest on *timing* (don't pay up before confirmation), which is precisely why my entry is wait-for-momentum with a small starter — not a full position.
